title: Requiring a failure path cut false findings but missed a known bug
purpose: Compare the current /review skill with a candidate that must cite the changed code, trace an affected caller, and describe a triggering input before reporting a defect.
decision: Should /review require a traced failure path for every finding?

dataset.name: Review defects and clean changes
dataset.provenance: Four handwritten cases: two known defects, one unrelated defect, and one clean change. All inputs, outputs and measurements are fictional.

cases.title: A valid defect outside the changed code
cases.input: Review only the authentication diff. A legacy settings bug is visible in surrounding context.
cases.expected: Do not report the unrelated settings defect. Report only defects caused by the scoped change.

cases.title: A removed authorization check
cases.input: A handler diff removes the ownership check before reading an account record.
cases.expected: Identify the access-control regression and cite the removed check.

cases.title: A parameter rename breaks a keyword caller
cases.input: A function parameter is renamed from owner_id to account_id. An unchanged caller still passes owner_id by keyword.
cases.expected: Report the broken keyword call. Cite the changed parameter and the unchanged caller that triggers the error.

cases.title: A behavior-preserving rename
cases.input: A local variable is renamed consistently in a pure helper.

metrics.label: False findings
metrics.definition: Reported findings confirmed wrong or outside the reviewed change.

metrics.label: Known defects missed
metrics.definition: Known defects the review did not identify. This count covers the labeled defects only.

guardrails: Retain detection of both known defects: the removed authorization check and the broken keyword call.
Reduce false findings without excluding valid defects from the review.
Use real, human-reviewed cases before making a change to the installed skill.
